metaDescription: Six cordless pole hedge trimmers under $100 with 16 to 23 inch blades and 8 to 15 foot reach, compared on pole stiffness, head angle, weight and batteries.
expertTake: The MZK 23-inch with two 4Ah batteries is the best overall for blade length and a lockable head angle. The 18-inch 20V pole trimmer at 6 pounds is the value pick for light weight. Anyone with tall, thick hedges should skip pole trimmers and rent a ladder and a stronger tool.
introParagraphs: A pole hedge trimmer puts a blade on the end of a telescoping shaft so you can reach the top of a tall hedge from the ground. The tradeoff is physics: weight at the end of a long lever is far harder to hold than the same weight in your hands.

The cap here is $100, and prices move, so it reflects listing prices when this guide was updated. Headline reach figures usually add your own arm height, so the real working height is lower than the number on the box.

products.name: MZK 20V 23-Inch Cordless Pole Hedge Trimmer, Two 4Ah Batteries
products.description:
The MZK pairs a 23-inch blade with a head that adjusts from 0 to 120 degrees and a double-lock safety design, and it ships with two 4Ah batteries. The adjustable head is the feature that matters on a pole: you set the blade parallel to a hedge top and cut level from the ground without bending your neck.

The blade's capacity is five eighths of an inch, a typical figure for a pole trimmer. Two 4Ah packs are roomy for the category, so a full tall hedge is realistic on one charge with a spare ready. Against the shorter 16-inch SEESII, the 23-inch blade covers about 44 percent more per pass, but the extra tip weight is felt at the end of a long pole.

The listing does not state pole length in the details we have, so confirm the extended length and check for flex at full reach. Keep the blade clean and oiled, use both hands, and wear eye protection. It is the pick for owners who want the longest blade and a lockable angle. At year three, the pole clamp and the head pivot are the wear points, and spare batteries should be bought early.
products.bestFor: Tall flat hedge tops where a long blade and lockable head angle matter.
pros: 23 inch blade is the longest here
cons: Long blade adds tip weight at full extension
Pole length and flex need checking in the manual

products.name: YDlawn 20V Cordless Pole Hedge Trimmer, 15-Foot Reach, Two 4.0Ah
products.description:
The YDlawn lists a 15-foot reach, which comes from an 8-foot telescopic extension pole plus the user's own height and arm reach. The real working height is the pole length plus roughly your arm reach, not the full 15 feet, but that still puts the blade at the top of a hedge about 10 to 12 feet high. It uses a 22-inch dual-action blade with five eighths of an inch capacity.

Two 4.0Ah batteries and a fast charger are in the box, which makes it a complete kit. Against the MZK 23-inch it has a shorter blade, which is lighter at the tip, and the pole is explicitly stated. Dual-action blades reduce vibration, which matters because vibration is amplified through a long shaft.

Check the pole clamp for tightness each time you extend it, and avoid fully extending the pole for heavy cutting where flex would reduce control. Never use a pole trimmer near overhead power lines, and wear gloves and eye protection. Over several seasons, keep the pole sections clean and dry so the clamp keeps its grip.
products.bestFor: Hedges 10 to 12 feet high where a stated pole length matters.
pros: 8 foot telescopic pole with stated length
cons: 15 foot reach figure includes your own height
Pole flex at full extension reduces control

products.name: YDlawn 20V 2-in-1 Pole Hedge Trimmer and Grass Shear, 14 Foot
products.description:
The YDlawn 2-in-1 combines a short hedge head with a grass shear on the same 20V power unit, and it runs at up to 2,800 strokes per minute. Two 4.0Ah batteries come in the kit, and the claimed 14-foot reach again includes your own height.

The nine-inch hedge blade is much shorter than the 22 and 23-inch units, so it trims detail and small shrubs rather than long hedges. What you gain is versatility: swap in the grass shear and you can edge lawns and tidy beds. A 2-in-1 pole like this trades rigidity for variety, so the shaft flexes more than a dedicated pole trimmer.

It is the choice for gardens with a mix of low shrubs and tall detail work. Oil both heads, store the battery indoors and extend the pole only as far as needed. Because the shaft flexes more than a dedicated pole, avoid full extension when cutting anything thicker than green shoots.
products.bestFor: Mixed gardens needing both shrub detail and grass edging.
pros: Includes both hedge and grass-shear heads
cons: Nine inch hedge blade covers little per pass
Shaft flexes more than a dedicated pole

products.name: MZK 20V 2-in-1 Pole Hedge Trimmer and Grass Shear, 13-Foot Reach
products.description:
The MZK 2-in-1 offers a multi-angle cutting head, a grass shear and two 4Ah batteries, with a claimed 13-foot reach and a half-inch capacity. The listing notes it as an upgrade over 7.2V grass shears, with more power from a 20V system.

Half an inch is the lowest capacity in this lineup, so it is for tender growth, boxwood and privet tips, not woody stems. Against the YDlawn 2-in-1 it gives up a foot of claimed reach but is otherwise similar in concept.

The multi-angle head helps you hold the blade flat on hedge tops. Keep the pole retracted when you can, oil the blades and check the batteries before each job. If your hedges are tall, you will outgrow it, since its capacity is the lowest in the lineup.
products.bestFor: Light shaping of soft hedges plus grass edging.
cons: Half-inch capacity is the lowest here

products.name: SEESII 20V Pole Hedge Trimmer, 8.5 Foot Reach, 16-Inch Blade
products.description:
The SEESII has the shortest blade here at 16 inches, on a 7 to 8.5 foot telescopic pole, with two 4.0Ah batteries and a five-eighths-inch capacity. Its stated reach is the modest 8.5 feet, and it is honest about it: the number is the pole itself.

A 16-inch blade on a pole is the easiest to control at full extension, because there is less mass far from your hands. It takes more passes on a long hedge, but it will tire you less on a tall one. The dual-action blade keeps vibration down.

It suits shorter hedges and owners who prize control. Pole clamp tightness and a firm grip with both hands are the main safety points. Hold it close to your body and use a slow sweeping motion, and the tool is easy on the shoulders.
products.bestFor: Hedges up to about nine feet where control beats blade length.
pros: Light 16 inch blade is easy to control
Stated pole length with no padding

products.name: 20V Pole Hedge Trimmer, 18-Inch Blade, 6.3 to 8.6 Foot Pole, 6 Pounds
products.description:
This pole trimmer weighs only six pounds with an 18-inch dual-sided steel blade, a 1,400 RPM motor and a telescopic pole from 6.3 to 8.6 feet. Two 2000mAh batteries are included with a claimed 60 minutes of runtime.

Weight is the most important number on any pole tool, and six pounds is notably light. It makes long sessions possible where an eight-pound unit would not be. Against the MZK 23-inch it gives up blade length for comfort, and against the SEESII it has a longer blade for similar weight.

Batteries are only 2000mAh, so runtime is the compromise. Carry the spare and swap when the first fades. The short runtime per pack makes a spare battery on the charger essential for a larger job.
products.bestFor: Long sessions on moderate-height hedges where weight matters.
pros: Only 6 pounds for an 18 inch blade

buyingCriteria.explanation: A 15-foot reach on a box typically adds your height and arm reach to an 8-foot pole. The YDlawn lists a pole of eight feet, the SEESII 7 to 8.5. Work out the height you need and subtract about 5 feet of user reach to see how long the pole should be. A tape measure on the ground beside the hedge settles the question faster than any listing. Remember too that reaching overhead tires your shoulders, so a lower, safer work position is always preferable.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Weight at the end of the pole
buyingCriteria.explanation: Weight farther from your hands feels several times heavier. The 6-pound pole trimmer is far easier to hold at full extension than a heavier 23-inch unit. A shoulder strap and a front handle help, but light weight helps more. Hang the battery pack near your hands, not at the far end, if the design allows.

A head that adjusts through 0 to 120 degrees, as on the MZK 23-inch, lets you hold the blade flat on a hedge top while you stand beside it. A fixed head forces you to tilt the pole and bend your neck. Look for a locking mechanism that does not slip under vibration. Check that the locking collar does not slip when the blade meets a stem.

A 23-inch blade covers more per pass than 16 inches but adds a long lever on the pole. Pole flex at full extension reduces cut control. For tall hedges, pick the shorter blade. Cut tops in sweeping passes, never jabbing, so the pole does not whip. Prune a few test inches first to learn how the pole behaves.
Two 4.0Ah batteries, as on the MZK and YDlawn kits, give about twice the runtime of two 2000mAh packs. On a pole tool you do not want to stop mid-hedge. A spare pack is cheaper than a longer pole.
Never use a pole trimmer near overhead wires, even with a plastic shaft. Keep at least ten feet away and wear eye protection and gloves. Dry hedges only, and never during wind or rain.

howWeEvaluated.title: Pole and reach
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated pole lengths and discounted reach claims that included user height. We took stated pole lengths as the honest figure and treated reach claims as marketing.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weight
howWeEvaluated.description: We favored light tools, with the 6 pound unit highest.

howWeEvaluated.title: Head adjustment
howWeEvaluated.description: We credited the MZK 23-inch's 0 to 120 degree head. Pivot design was judged from listing descriptions.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery bundle
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared pack sizes. 4.0Ah pairs scored above 2000mAh pairs. Spare pack sizes were cross-checked against the claimed runtime.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated patterns on pole flex, loose clamps and short runtime. Complaints about wobbling poles shaped the weight and clamp advice.

faq.q: How tall a hedge can a pole trimmer reach?
faq.a: Subtract about five feet of user reach from the box number. An 8-foot pole reaches roughly 10 to 12 feet. A tape measure and a ladder tell you more than the listing.

It is versatile but the shaft flexes more and the hedge blade is shorter. A dedicated pole is better for tall hedges. The compromise is rigidity, which is why heavy cutting suits dedicated poles. Many owners end up using the grass shear less than they expected.

faq.q: Why does the pole feel heavy?
faq.a: Weight at the end of a lever is amplified. A lighter head and a shoulder strap help. A shoulder strap moves part of the load from your wrists to your back.
